items.title: Norris wins wet-dry-wet São Paulo race; final order reflects penalties
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Norris won the 71-lap race in 1:35:23.504, 14.602 seconds ahead of Verstappen, with Hadjar third. The final classification places Lawson seventh and Leclerc eighth after Leclerc's post-race penalty.
items.why_it_matters: The provisional track order changed after the stewards' decisions; use the final classification for results and points.

items.title: Mercedes clinch a ninth Constructors' title at Interlagos
items.summary: Russell finished fourth and Antonelli fifth, enough to secure Mercedes' ninth Constructors' Championship. Formula1.com reports this is the team's first title since 2021 and leaves it joint with Williams on nine, behind McLaren and Ferrari.
items.why_it_matters: Both championships are settled: Antonelli had already secured the Drivers' title at Mexico, so focus on the confirmed result rather than live title permutations.

sources.label: Formula1.com on Mercedes' title and rivals' reactions

items.title: Intermediates bracketed the soft-tyre phase as rain returned
items.summary: Pirelli reports every starter began on Intermediates and all drivers used both Intermediates and Softs. Norris completed Soft stints of 33 and 13 laps before changing back to Intermediates as rain returned; Russell and Leclerc each ran 45 laps on one Soft set and ten on a second. Pirelli observed mainly thermal degradation with some graining on the drying track.
items.why_it_matters: These are observed race stints, distinct from the pre-race remaining-set inventory and strategy forecasts.

sources.label: Pirelli's official São Paulo race report

items.title: Vasseur attributes Ferrari's difficult weekend to tyre-temperature struggles
items.summary: Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur said the team struggled to keep both Intermediate and Soft tyres in the right temperature window. He estimated that effect could reach roughly half a second; Leclerc and Hamilton finished eighth and ninth.
items.why_it_matters: The half-second figure is Vasseur's assessment, not an independent telemetry measurement or a complete explanation of the result.

sources.label: Formula1.com on Vasseur and Ferrari's tyre struggles
